A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Learning to Bet for Horizon-Aware Anytime-Valid Testing. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original dynamic-programming calculations, DQN training, Monte Carlo rejection probabilities, confidence-sequence experiments, and betting trajectories in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original distribution-transfer experiments, real-data evaluations, ablations, sensitivity tests, and null-calibration results.

M1.justification: The main three-action DQN and its architecture remain unchanged. Sections 4.4 and F.1 add trained DQN-EB and DQN-U variants with early-rejection rewards, while F.4 tests an expanded nine-action policy. These are limited extensions of the existing learning procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Beta/Beta-mixture experiments, v2 evaluates transfer to logit-normal distributions and six real-data sources: three DNA methylation samples and three relative-humidity stations. It also adds Bernoulli-family training and evaluation, using a separately trained policy.

E2.justification: The external comparator set remains empirical Kelly, Linear-ε, Hedge, STaR-Bets, and STaR-Hoeffding. Figure 6 adds DQN-EB and DQN-U as internal comparators in the retained Beta-mixture setting, and Figure 15 compares the original DQN with its nine-action variant.

E3.justification: v2 adds empirical-distribution resampling protocols with N=100 and null controls, a matched-budget action-space comparison, evaluation at N=250, 300, and 350, and retraining/evaluation at α=0.01. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original experiments and main training settings remain intact.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds reward-function and action-space ablations, distribution-transfer tests, deadline and significance-level sensitivity experiments, and explicit Type-I error checks. These address design choices and robustness questions beyond v1's training curves and qualitative trajectories, which are retained.

E5.justification: The new real-data curves use the existing practice of estimating frequencies over 5,000 trials. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across independently trained DQN seeds. The fixed-seed checkpoint evaluation remains unchanged; null-calibration curves are new outcomes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained, while Figures 6–18 add substantial new findings. These include improved power on additional distribution families, the highest deadline rejection probability in five of six real-data cases, earlier rejection versus terminal-power tradeoffs from reward shaping, and no overall improvement from nine actions.

T1.justification: Equation 1 generalizes deadline power to expected utility E[u(τ)1{τ≤N}] for nonnegative, nonincreasing u, with an expected-wealth constraint at bounded stopping times. The subsequent analysis specializes to u=1. The Bellman recursion, principal theoretical results, and Appendix A–B proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and headline contributions remain the finite-horizon control formulation, three-regime betting theory, and a universal DQN that improves deadline power and confidence sequences while preserving validity. The expanded experiments primarily provide additional support for these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of reward tradeoffs, optimization difficulty with larger action spaces, transfer beyond training distributions, and use of the Type-I error budget. It explicitly limits real-data evidence to resampled marginal distributions and adds an interpretability limitation. The conclusion replaces the Beta-only experimental limitation with broader remaining distributional questions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, GEO sample identifiers, humidity station/date information, humidity normalization and resampling instructions, and specifications for the new policy variants. The original implementation descriptions, architecture, hardware information, and Table 1 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Koning and Van Meer (2026), discussing their Doob-martingale construction and distinguishing this paper's restriction to multiplicative betting processes. Other reference changes largely update metadata for existing works rather than introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, expands Section 4.4, adds an Impact Statement, and organizes Appendix F into nine subsections. The original training and trajectory subsections move to F.8–F.9. Most existing prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds thirteen multipanel figures, Figures 6–18, displaying new comparisons, data histograms, calibration curves, and ablations. Original Figures 1–5 remain, while v1 Figures 6–9 become Figures 19–22. Table 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's explicit Beta-only validation limitation through transfer tests on logit-normal and six real empirical distributions, alongside separately trained Bernoulli experiments. Reward/action ablations and null-calibration checks also make the design choices and empirical behavior better supported. Real-data evidence remains limited to i.i.d. resampling, but the broader validation materially strengthens the paper while retaining its original theory and results.
